title: Generate Failure-Diagnosed Curricula That Improve Held-Out Agent Capabilities
target_platform: Local deterministic curriculum scheduler; evaluating-agent-work; cheap learner (ceiling 750k tokens)
hypothesis: A curriculum selected from diagnosed failure categories and prerequisite relationships will: (a) reach 80% held-out task success using >= 30% fewer learning episodes than both random selection and weakest-category-first selection; (b) end with <= 3 percentage points regression on previously mastered categories; and (c) achieve these results within 60 learning episodes.
falsification_criteria: Fail if target is not reached within 60 episodes, episode savings are below 30%, or retention fails. Choosing easier evaluation tasks after observing failures invalidates the run.
experiment: Use 6 task families with hidden evaluation cases and known prerequisites. Each learning episode runs one bounded experiment and updates a procedure or memory artifact. Keep model weights fixed to isolate curriculum selection. Evaluate frozen snapshots at preregistered intervals.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Frontier models are excluded; curriculum scheduling is deterministic graph traversal and diagnostic categorization.

related_missions.MISSION-014: EXTENDS: shifts from pure information-theoretic gain to active capability acquisition.
related_missions.MISSION-011: SUPPLIES DATA TO: generates structured learning sequences for sovereign fine-tuning.
related_missions.MISSION-043: SUPPLIES DATA TO: orders domain updates to minimize catastrophic forgetting in sequential LoRA adapters.

resources: isolated fixture memory stores; max 750k inference tokens across 60 episodes
